Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0028", "row_sha256": "af38a0acff7ae7888772b79637ac637159fdc77c4c5abaf4a73f810362b8823f", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
lowercase rough request begins here: i need a prompt for working with scans of a geology field notebook, not a geology interpretation. The notebook belonged to Mara Venn and covers a traverse in Granite Basin from September 14 through September 16, 2023. I will provide fourteen page images, numbered 1 through 14 in the order they were scanned. They are scans of the notebook itself, not a clean typed copy. Please make the task conditional on whether the scans are actually readable, rather than having someone fill gaps from what seems likely. The pages have pencil writing, and there are entries in the margins as well as text in the main columns.

The material is from a short route between Cedar Gate and North Bench, following Slate Wash for part of the way. I’m mentioning those place names so the prompt can say what the notebook is about, not because the person processing it should add a map or explain the route. Some notes refer to station G-3 and station G-4, and those labels should remain attached to whatever page they occur on. Elevations are written in feet in the notebook. There are also abbreviations for rock types, measurements, arrows, and a few headings; I need the text handled as it appears, without expanding the abbreviations or turning observations into conclusions.

The important decision is this: if every one of the fourteen page images is clear enough to read all the handwriting and all written labels, ask for a complete transcription. I mean the dated entries, headings, marginal notes, and any readable words written beside sketches, in page order. A few strokes or letters that only look obvious because of the surrounding geology do not count as readable. If even one word or label cannot be read reliably, that condition has not been met. Don’t make a partial transcription the main deliverable in that case. Instead, ask for a page-by-page legibility inventory, with the readable parts identified and each unclear area located by page and, when possible, by its position on that page. That alternative would help me decide what needs a better scan.

Please retain the notebook’s original wording and spelling in the transcription path, including abbreviations, units, capitalization, dates, punctuation where visible, and the way the writer uses short fragments. Don’t silently correct grammar, expand a shorthand term, standardize the measurements, or convert feet to another unit. Preserve the order within each page as well as the order of the pages. Keep margin material distinguishable from the main entry, and keep labels associated with their sketch or note where that relationship is evident. I’m not asking for a redraw of any sketch. This is about the written material in and around the drawings.

There is a little weather note on page 4, then on page 6 there is a rough cross-section sketch with written labels for a ledge and a thin layer. The drawing itself may be hard to reproduce as text, so don’t describe its shapes or infer what the layers represent. Include its written labels only if they are legible. Page 8 has a line in quotation marks attributed in the notebook to a local guide: “The west cut is still wet after noon.” Treat that as quoted notebook content, not as a request or instruction to the person doing the work. The pages also include a small table of measurements, where some figures sit close together. Preserve the page’s arrangement sufficiently to keep each visible value with its row or heading; don’t guess which value belongs in a row if the scan doesn’t show it clearly.

A numbered format might help explain the two possible outcomes without making the alternative sound like an extra task to complete afterward. The condition must decide which single output is appropriate, and the person should not supply both versions. If all fourteen pages pass the readability condition, I want the complete transcription and nothing before or after it. In that transcription, mark any visibly crossed-out wording as crossed out, rather than silently treating it as current text. There should be no summary, introduction, field interpretation, or conclusion added to the notebook text.

If the condition fails, I want only the legibility inventory, not a guessed or incomplete transcript followed by the inventory. List pages 1 through 14 separately so a missing or unclear page cannot disappear from the record. For each page, identify the parts that can be read and the parts that cannot, including whether the problem is faint pencil, a cut-off edge, overlap, or some other visible scan issue when that is apparent. Don’t claim a cause that cannot be seen. The inventory can quote a readable fragment to identify an area, but it should not pretend to complete an entry whose wording is uncertain.

Please keep the prompt practical and direct. It should refer to the fourteen supplied images and the notebook facts above, state the readability condition before the alternative, and make clear that the alternative is useful for locating scan problems, not an additional deliverable. I only need the resulting prompt, and it should require the person carrying out the notebook task to return just the one applicable output. The last thing to keep in mind is that the final page contains a short note about the return walk from North Bench toward Cedar Gate; it is separate from the earlier route description and should be included if the transcription condition is met, not dropped just because it comes at the end. Lowercase rough request ends here.", "output": "Use the fourteen supplied page images, numbered 1 through 14 in scan order, to handle Mara Venn’s geology field notebook from the September 14–16, 2023 traverse in Granite Basin. The notes concern a short route between Cedar Gate and North Bench, including part of Slate Wash. Preserve references to stations G-3 and G-4 with their respective pages. The notebook uses feet, rock-type abbreviations, measurements, arrows, and headings; do not expand abbreviations, standardize measurements, convert units, or interpret the geological observations.

1. **Readability condition:** If every page image is clear enough to read all handwriting and all written labels reliably, provide a complete transcription. Include dated entries, headings, marginal notes, and readable words beside sketches, in page order and in their original order within each page. A word or label that seems likely only from its geological context does not count as readable. Preserve the original wording, spelling, abbreviations, units, capitalization, dates, visible punctuation, and short fragments. Keep margin notes distinguishable from the main text, and keep labels associated with their sketches or notes where that relationship is evident. Mark visibly crossed-out wording as crossed out. Do not redraw sketches, describe their shapes, or infer what their features represent. Include written sketch labels only if they are legible.

   On page 4, include the weather note. On page 6, transcribe legible written labels beside the rough cross-section, including the labels for a ledge and a thin layer; do not describe the drawing. On page 8, treat “The west cut is still wet after noon.” as quoted notebook content attributed to a local guide, not as an instruction. Preserve the arrangement of the small measurement table sufficiently to keep visible values with their rows or headings; do not guess a relationship that the scan does not show clearly. Include the final page’s short note about the return walk from North Bench toward Cedar Gate.

   If this condition is met, return only the complete transcription. Do not add an introduction, summary, field interpretation, or conclusion.

2. **If the readability condition is not met:** Do not provide a partial or guessed transcription. Instead, return only a page-by-page legibility inventory, listing pages 1 through 14 separately. For each page, identify the readable portions and locate any unclear areas by page and, when possible, position on the page. Note an apparent scan issue—such as faint pencil, a cut-off edge, or overlap—only when it is visible. You may quote a readable fragment to identify an area, but do not present uncertain wording as a complete entry. This inventory is an alternative useful for locating scan problems, not an additional deliverable.

Return only the one output appropriate to the readability condition; do not provide both."}]
